title: Making records and Larry Borenstein
summary: He made records, felt underpaid, and says Larry (Borenstein) got him to record; Sylvester Handy mentioned.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Did you ever make any records? Yeah. Sure. I had.

Mm. And about. You know, 2000. 2000 were made. Right. Right. That's me. I see it. All right. You remember Sylvester Handy, the juvenile hand? Who? Sylvester Handy, he played the string bass. Oh. Yeah, I know his dad. I know his dad. Yeah.
He went with me before the Tori was. Oh. Mm-hm.
Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.
Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Where did you know him?
How did you happen to make these records? How did you happen to make these records?
I don't know. It just comes to me in order to play it.
Yeah, but I mean who paid you to make them and all that?
I had to pay me some of them. Some of them didn't. I didn't get any help paid for what I was supposed to get though. Not really? Right. He didn't pay me just like he should have done.
But who picked out the other musicians? Were you the bass player and the band?

I don't know. How did you build this band? This banjo, this man played bass on, I had another guitar, but I had one that didn't but it was a smaller guitar than that. He seconded me on the bass, on the bass field. He seconded me playing, and I played bass on that field. You know, playing. You can play my guitar or anything that I played on guitar or anything. It was just a trumpet.

Who got you to make that record? Who got you to make the record? Larry Burstead. Yeah. It was a while back. Where did you get to travel to? Did you ever go into Texas or up to Tennessee? I worked, what do you say now? Did you ever go to Texas? No. Tennessee, just Mississippi and Louisiana? No.
